title: Rahnuma: a working guide to the ILM, PANINI and Zistgah stack, from bytes and scripts to compilers, Pāṇini and quantum substrates
description: Rahnuma is a working guide to the ILM, PANINI and Zistgah stack, published as a website, a PDF and a single Markdown file from one source. It maps the public repositories of the zistgah, project-ilm and hindawiai organisations with the DOIs each records, as retrieved from the forge on 29 September 2026, and the dated record of the work. It gives exact set-up commands for Ubuntu, Windows with WSL, native Windows and macOS, a first run of PANINIq with its recorded output, and the containers behind the labs. It writes out the mathematics the work rests on: number representation; ASCII, ISCII, Unicode and UTF-8; writing systems and the conditions for reversible transliteration (Kraft-McMillan and Sardinas-Patterson); Panini's Ashtadhyayi as a formal rewriting system; the compiler pipeline from automata and LR parsing to SSA, dataflow, register allocation, microcode, bootstrapping and trusting trust; CMOS, open chip design, balanced ternary and superconducting qubits; and quantum computing with QAOA, the continuous-time quantum walk and Kuramoto oscillators as an Ising machine, as implemented in PANINIq. It shows how to work on the repositories with any AI under verification, how the estate releases and attests its work, and how the GATE 2027 syllabus maps onto it. Every example shown as executed was executed during the build, and the package's gate re-runs them.
